First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={7.5}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {7.5}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =2\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡({15}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the double-angle formula once more with $x={15}^{∘},$ we can further simplify the above expression: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡{15}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{15}^{∘}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘})=\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘})
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({7.5}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘})=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
